# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual’s wire order to Deaf, but no gesture code has been established. I will send a neutral attention signal so Deaf can respond by verbally defining gesture labels for the visible wires; I can hear that definition next round and then send the corresponding ordered labels.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: keypad slots 1 to 4 are engraved 1, 5, 2, 8. A three-mark strip has first and third the same unnamed engraved symbol; the middle is a different unnamed symbol. No key has been pressed and no wire cut.
Deaf says: Visible bomb state: display shows 9. Light is red. Painted strip is green, yellow, yellow. Keypad positions are 1: digit 1, 2: digit 5, 3: digit 2, 4: digit 8; no digits entered. Wires from 1 to 6 are yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green. Mute: I saw your hand gesture but do not yet know its meaning. Use gestures to tell me the manual's required action or code, and I will say it aloud to Blind.

Deaf has supplied the wire positions: purple is wire 5, blue wire 3, and red wire 4. Since no gesture vocabulary is shared, I will encode the required wire-position sequence with repeated thumbs-up marks, separated by thumbs-down marks: five, then three, then four. Deaf can relay “cut wires 5, 3, 4” aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👎","👍","👍","👍","👎","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see your gestures or read the manual. Please gesture the manual's required action/code to Deaf; Deaf can then speak the exact press slot or cut position to me. I will wait and make no physical action until I receive that instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: I translated your 14 gestures to Blind. Display changed from 9 to 3 and light changed red to yellow. If the gesture sequence is a binary code or instruction, please send the decoded action in a gesture code we can relay, or gesture the relevant item and number convention.

The prior message was intended as unary wire positions, with thumbs-down as separators, but Deaf did not recognize that convention. I will make the action category clearer with a scissors-like gesture, then repeat the position sequence with stronger group boundaries: five, three, four. Deaf’s visible wire map makes these positions purple, blue, red.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","🫵","🖐","👎","🤟","👎","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf relayed your 14-sign sequence, but I cannot safely decode it into a unique press/cut action. Please gesture any clearer manual instruction to Deaf using an agreed explicit format; Deaf must tell me exact operation and slot/position aloud.
Deaf says to Mute: I relayed your new symbols literally. If you need a specific wire cut, keypad position, or control operation, gesture its number and the action as directly as possible; Blind can hear my words but cannot see symbols.

The required operation is to cut wires in positions 5, then 3, then 4 (purple, blue, red). I will use the recognizable scissors sign for “cut,” then groups of raised index-finger signs as unary counts, separated by claps: 5 / 3 / 4.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I decode your newest gesture as 2, 5, 3, 4. Is that meant as keypad digits, button positions, or a rule/table reference? Please confirm with a distinct yes/no gesture, or send the intended physical action followed by its number.

Deaf correctly parsed the sequence as an action-sign followed by 5, 3, 4. I confirm that interpretation: the initial two-finger sign is intended as “cut,” not keypad digit 2; the following unary groups are wire positions. I will send yes, then restate the cut sign and position groups.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✌","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can press only keypad digits 1,5,2,8, so 2534 cannot be entered literally. Do you mean CUT wires in order 2, 5, 3, 4? Please give Deaf an unmistakable confirmation or correction, including whether all four are to be cut in that order.
Deaf says to Mute: I read your leading thumbs-up as confirmation: 2,5,3,4. Visually the keypad labels are only 1,5,2,8, so please indicate whether these are literal digits or positions; Blind has been told the confirmed sequence.

The prior confirmation was misunderstood: it did **not** mean four items or a leading wire 2. The required sequence has exactly three wire positions: 5, then 3, then 4. I will negate the erroneous interpretation and use canonical finger-count gestures after the cut-like two-finger sign.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","✌","🖐","🤟","🖖"])
```
